front.title: Verification Defect Quarantine for Protocol Conformance Systems

abstract.t: Protocol conformance systems commonly treat a published test vector as an oracle. When the oracle itself is malformed, internally inconsistent, ambiguous, or arithmetically false, an implementation can be penalized for rejecting the defect or can be falsely promoted for reproducing it. This document defines Verification Defect Quarantine (VDQ), a transport-neutral receipt and fail-closed state model for separating the status of the tested subject from the demonstrated fault-detection behavior of the verifier. VDQ records reproducible counterexamples, quarantines affected normative vectors from assurance promotion, preserves INDETERMINATE when a defect cannot yet be reproduced, and supports append-only supersession when a specification is corrected. VDQ does not amend an Internet-Draft or RFC, does not replace the RFC Editor errata process, and does not by itself establish implementation security.
